label: AI Agents + Automations
title: Run DeepSeek Harness free on your own computer
body:
If you came here from the DeepSeek Harness video, this one's for you.

Quick version of the setup:
1. Install Node.js, then run: npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
2. Skip the DeepSeek key it asks for. You don't need one.
3. Connect a model. OpenRouter with about $10 of credit, or Ollama for 100% free and local.
4. For Ollama, use "Add custom provider" (not "Add provider") with http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
5. Turn on the Claude Code sub-agent plugin so it hands long jobs to the Claude plan you already pay for.

My honest take: it doesn't replace Claude Code today. It lets you build a harness shaped the way you work.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xprBcuJKDA

Did you get it running? Local or OpenRouter?

label: AI Agents + Automations
title: Hermes Agent: the setup notes from the video
body:
The Hermes video said the setup notes would be in here, so here they are.

How I think about it: Claude Code is the specialist you open inside a project. Hermes runs on its own machine, remembers every session in files you can open, and keeps working after you close the laptop.

The short path:
1. Install it from hermes-agent.nousresearch.com (terminal or the desktop app)
2. Settings > Providers, connect your Claude or ChatGPT plan
3. Tell it about yourself so it saves that to memory
4. Turn one task into a skill
5. Schedule a job that messages you on Slack
6. Run it free with a local model: ollama launch hermes

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzwYKfSxToU

If you set it up, what's the first job you're giving it?

title: Build an AI agent in 5 steps (no code)
body:
This is the agent that researches my niche before I sit down. It pulls the top content from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and X and hands me a brief with ideas.

The 5 steps:
1. Pick where to build it (I use Claude Code)
2. Describe the agent and let Claude write it
3. Give it tools with the Apify MCP server
4. Grill it with Matt Pocock's /grilling skill until it holds up
5. Put it on a schedule with /schedule

The finished skill is free: https://github.com/tylerprogramming/claude-skills/tree/main/social-me

title: One MCP server, six apps, zero code
body:
If MCP still sounds like jargon, start with this one.

I connected Claude Code to Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Docs, Slack and ClickUp through one gateway in arcade.dev. No code and no OAuth to fight. You click the tools you want, copy one command into Claude Code, and sign in.

Then one prompt summarized my emails with a partner in Gmail, wrote a Google Doc, saved it to a Drive folder, and messaged me on Slack.

What you need:
- Claude Code
- A free arcade.dev account: https://www.arcade.dev/
- The apps you want to connect

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uEUP4iHJO1Q

title: I edit videos by talking to Claude Code now
body:
Captions, silence cuts, transitions and B-roll, all by asking in plain English.

It runs on HyperFrames, HeyGen's free open-source video tool, which installs a set of skills into Claude Code. No editing software.

What you need:
- Claude Code
- HyperFrames: https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes
- Node.js and FFmpeg (both free)

Honest note: it's not one-click magic. The good results take some back and forth. Expect a conversation.

The step-by-step guide is in the Classroom under YouTube Library.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdvi2ooarDc

title: Run my Opus 5 benchmark on your own machine
body:
I ran the same 6 prompts through Opus 4.8, Opus 5 and Fable 5 and put the cost next to each one.

The catch: Opus 5 is half Fable's price per token, but it wrote 2 to 4 times more code on builds. Half the price per token didn't always mean a cheaper job. In my runs 4.8 was the cheapest and fastest.

The model-bench skill is free, so you can run the same tests on your Claude plan with no API key:
https://github.com/tylerprogramming/claude-skills/tree/main/model-bench

The step-by-step guide is in the Classroom under YouTube Library.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J5lkE_jBEko

Run one test and post your numbers. Are you seeing the same thing?

title: A 30-second product ad from one photo
body:
One product photo and one prompt, and the ElevenLabs Flows Agent built the whole ad: images, video clips, voiceover, music and the final edit.

Then I changed it by talking to the agent and swapped in a new product to reuse the same flow.

Good to know:
- It's paid. My ad used about 32,000 credits, so the Creator plan is the realistic one.
- It's not really one prompt. Expect to iterate.
- This was a paid partnership, and the link below is my partner link.
